item.title: Estimation-Aware Reachability Extends Safety Verification to Noisy Robot Estimates
item.description:
Estimation-Aware Reachability Extends Safety Verification to Noisy Robot Estimates

A new paper titled “Estimation-Aware Reachability” extends Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability to account for the noisy estimates used by real robots.

🔍 Overview

Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability computes the states from which a system can be kept safe under worst-case disturbances, but it assumes the state is known exactly. Real robots, however, act on noisy estimates whose uncertainty evolves with their motion. This work extends Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability to the robot’s belief, estimate, and uncertainty.

🧩 How it works

The formulation treats unexpected measurements as a bounded adversary and enlarges the unsafe set by the current uncertainty. This ensures that certified states are safe with a prescribed probability.

⚙️ Key details

  • The formulation is compatible with existing solvers.
  • In simulation, the resulting safety filters nearly eliminate the collisions of certainty-equivalent HJ.
  • The approach is less conservative than equally safe uncertainty-padding baselines.

🚀 Availability

The implementation code is available at the provided URL.

item.title: OpenClaw Updates Memory Plugin with LanceDB for Persistent AI Context
item.description:
OpenClaw Updates Memory Plugin with LanceDB for Persistent AI Context

OpenClaw has released an update to its memory plugin, now enhanced with LanceDB for persistent, cross-session memory capabilities.

🔍 Overview

The plugin provides a brain that remembers across sessions, agents, and time. It stores preferences, decisions, and project context.

🧩 How it works

  • Classification: LLM-powered 6-category classification (profiles, preferences, entities, events, cases, patterns).
  • Retention: Weibull decay model ensures important memories stay while noise fades.
  • Retrieval: Hybrid Retrieval (Vector + BM25) fused with Cross-Encoder Reranking.
  • Automation: Relevant memories automatically surface before each reply.

⚙️ Key details

  • Version: v1.1.0-beta.10.
  • Architecture: Fully adapted for OpenClaw 2026.3+ new plugin architecture.
  • Hooks: Uses before_prompt_build hooks (replacing deprecated before_agent_start).
  • Isolation: Per-agent, per-user, and per-project memory boundaries.
  • CPU Requirement: CPU must support AVX instructions.
  • Compatibility: LanceDB native vector search may require AVX2 on some Linux x64 builds and can crash AVX-only CPUs with SIGILL.

🚀 Availability

  • Installation: Run npm i memory-lancedb-pro@beta.
  • Setup: Use the community-maintained setup script.
  • Configuration: Add the plugin’s install directory as an absolute path in plugins.load.paths in openclaw.json.
  • Post-Upgrade: Run openclaw doctor --fix after upgrading.
  • API: Supports OpenAI, Jina, Gemini, Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible API.
  • Fallback: Set retrieval.disableNativeCosine: true or MEMORY_LANCEDB_DISABLE_NATIVE_COSINE=1 to use a scoped row scan plus JavaScript cosine ranking.

item.title: COSI Framework for Statistical Functionals
item.description:
COSI Framework for Statistical Functionals

A new framework named COSI has been introduced for constructing confidence sets for statistical functionals.

🔍 Overview

COSI stands for COnfidence from Scale Invariance. It is a framework for constructing confidence sets for statistical functionals. The framework builds on HulC (Hull-based Confidence), which uses median unbiasedness to construct confidence sets from batch estimates.

🧩 How it works

The process involves dividing the data into batches, computing an estimate in each batch, and retaining each candidate parameter value for which the batch estimates pass a test of scale invariance.

⚙️ Key details

COSI uses scale-invariance properties shared by many common estimators. The resulting confidence sets are asymptotically valid under weaker assumptions than classical Wald and bootstrap procedures require. Additionally, their coverage can be closer to the nominal level in small samples.

💡 Why it matters

Applications include:

  • Robust inference for the mean
  • Regression coefficients in misspecified linear models
  • Tensor norms
  • Fréchet means

item.title: Curated List of AI/LLM Code Execution Sandboxes
item.description:
Curated List of AI/LLM Code Execution Sandboxes

A curated list of code-execution sandboxing solutions for AI/LLM agents has been released. The collection features various runtime environments designed to secure code execution for autonomous agents.

🔍 Overview

The list encompasses a wide array of sandboxing technologies, ranging from open-source cloud runtimes to commercial enterprise-grade solutions. It includes options for full cloud VMs, MicroVMs, and container-based environments.

⚙️ Key details

  • Boot Times: Solutions offer boot times ranging from milliseconds to 2 seconds.
  • Isolation Methods: Technologies include Firecracker microVMs, hardware-level isolation, and Kubernetes backends like gVisor and Kata.
  • SDK Support: Available SDKs include TypeScript, Python, Rust, and CLI tools.
  • Networking: Features include private overlay networking, fine-grained controls, and public preview URLs with no inbound ports.

🛡️ Security Features

  • Isolation: Hardware-level isolation via Firecracker microVMs and VM-level isolation.
  • Monitoring: Tamper-evident audit logs and action-level tracing.
  • Access Control: Host-enforced egress allowlists and API key injection by a host-side broker.
  • Encryption: End-to-end encryption is available.

🚀 Availability

  • Deployment: Options include an agent deployment framework with SDK decorators and one-click configuration.
  • Hosting: Solutions can be hosted on kosa8 Cloud, your own hosts, or locally on Mac, Linux, or Windows machines.
  • Access: SSH-accessible Linux boxes and full cloud VMs are available.

item.title: Nvidia Stops Selling Hopper AI Chips to China
item.description:
Nvidia Stops Selling Hopper AI Chips to China

Nvidia has stopped sending its advanced AI chips to China despite receiving approval from the White House in December last year. The company announced it is no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China.

🔍 Overview

The announcement was made by interim CEO Colette Kress during an earnings call on Tuesday. This marks a notable shift for the company, which, under former CEO Jensen Huang, fought for the right to ship its powerful Hopper architecture H200 chips to China.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Leadership Shift: The pivot comes after Jensen Huang stepped down from his position as Nvidia CEO last week following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, one with a woman suspected by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy.
  • Previous Approval: Nvidia had received approval from the White House to ship the chips in December last year.
  • Supply Chain Delays: Nvidia already faced difficulties around offloading the AI chips prior to this scandal. Reuters reported earlier this month that around 600,000 H200 chips were stuck in Hong Kong after Beijing withheld approval for large-scale imports.
  • Vetting Concerns: Concerns were raised about failings to properly vet Chinese companies that were approved to handle the H200 AI chips.

🚀 Availability

Nvidia is not selling any more AI chips to China. Colette Kress stated, “Our guidance does not have any licensed Hopper data center products included, and we are no longer shipping licenced Hopper data center products to China.”

💡 Why it matters

She did not explain why Nvidia was ceasing its H200 processor shipments or clarify whether Nvidia would pursue other business with China in the future. However, the move aligns with China’s efforts to reduce its dependency on US technology.

item.title: IFS Copperleaf Builds IONA with Databricks to Democratize Business Data Access
item.description:
IFS Copperleaf Builds IONA with Databricks to Democratize Business Data Access

IFS Copperleaf, a provider of Asset Investment Planning software, partnered with Databricks to build IONA, a platform designed to democratize access to business data and advanced analytics.

🤝 The Partnership

IFS Copperleaf and Databricks share a vision to rethink how employees interact with business data and make advanced analytics accessible to everyone. The team explored the Databricks Genie product family, specifically looking for AI cowork and conversational analytics features. IFS Copperleaf became a voice for advanced customers, sharing prototypes and feedback to help shape the future of Genie One, Genie Agents, and Genie Ontology.

“We would have moved on to build our own thing. But we made this partnership happen because we both had the same vision.”

🎯 The Challenge

IFS Copperleaf runs on many systems, from CRM and marketing platforms to support, contract and finance tools, each owned by a different part of the business. Lisa Richter, Director of Technology and AI at IFS Copperleaf, notes that even at a simplistic level, questions like “how many customers do we have?” are hard to answer due to siloed systems and inconsistent definitions.

🛠️ The Solution (IONA)

The goal was to create a foundation that is standardized, governed, and usable by business teams without waiting for a specialist. The team held it to three outcomes: faster decisions, grounded in trusted data, and no longer dependent on a specialist.

Instead of the textbook approach of cleaning every table, the team flipped the process. Finance and the marketing-to-sales funnel are fully modeled, while everything else answers directly on raw data. This allows data to become useful months sooner.

📈 Outcomes

Business users were immediately relieved and excited to have democratized access to data that had previously been limited to formal analysis or technical practitioners. Unlike generic AI tools, IONA, built on Genie and grounded in Genie Ontology, was designed to self-improve and prompt for additional information when needed.

As employees began working with IONA to refine its understanding of their business, IFS Copperleaf brought that real-world feedback to the Databricks team. This collaboration helped shape the future of the Genie platform.

“Five years ago, I’d have shut this down myself. Business users writing logic that changes the number the whole company sees, with no ticket, no sprint and no rel…”

item.title: Zephon: High-Performance Data Loading Library for AI Training
item.description:
Zephon: High-Performance Data Loading Library for AI Training

Zephon is a high-performance data loading library that separates what you train on from how data is loaded and transformed.

🧩 Overview

  • Supports online processing (tokenization, sequence packing, filtering, dynamic mixtures) rather than requiring expensive offline preprocessing.
  • Guarantees deterministic, reproducible output regardless of parallelism or hardware topology.

Supported Data Formats

Feature Description
zephon[cloud] Reading from S3, GCS, and Azure (s3://, gs://, az:// paths)
zephon[hf] Hugging Face datasets (hf:// paths), plus Parquet
zephon[parquet] Parquet shards
zephon[streaming] MosaicML Streaming / MDS shards (Python 3.11+)
zephon[litdata] LitData shards
zephon[vortex] Vortex shards (Python 3.11+)
zephon[array_record] ArrayRecord shards
zephon[lance] Lance datasets, one shard per fragment
zephon[ray] The experimental Ray runner

🔄 How it works

A Zephon pipeline has three parts: a Dataset that describes your data, a WorkSource that decides what to train on and in what order, and a Pipeline of operators that turns samples into training batches.

  1. Describe the data: A directory of JSONL, Parquet, MDS, LitData, Vortex, ArrayRecord, or Lance shards.
  2. Decide what to train on, and in what order.
  3. Turn samples into training batches.

Mixing datasets is a matter of adding them to the WorkSource with the proportions you want.

For example, to train on Parquet data in S3:

1

uv pip install "zephon[cloud,parquet]"

Note that running a pipeline with a cloud storage backend requires enabling the shard cache.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Requirements: Requires Python 3.10 or newer. Python 3.11+ is required for zephon[streaming] and zephon[vortex].
  • Tokenization: Tokenization uses Hugging Face tokenizers, so you will also want uv pip install transformers if following examples.
  • Integration: A Pipeline is a plain Python iterable, so it works with whatever training loop you have. It will also run inside a PyTorch DataLoader or torchdata StatefulDataLoader if your framework insists on one, although direct iteration is recommended.
  • State Management: You can save and restore a pipeline’s position alongside your model checkpoint:
1
2

state = pipeline.checkpoint() # store this with the model and optimizer state
pipeline.restore(state) # on resume, before iter

item.title: Diagram Design Agent Skill Generates HTML and SVG Diagrams for AI Coding Environments
item.description:
Diagram Design Agent Skill Generates HTML and SVG Diagrams for AI Coding Environments

A new agent skill named “diagram-design” has been released, enabling AI coding assistants to generate self-contained HTML and SVG diagrams in a user’s brand style.

🔍 Overview

The skill supports 48 diagram types and produces self-contained HTML + SVG files. It adheres to design constraints, including no shadows and no Mermaid.

🧩 How it works

The agent selects the diagram type, states its plan, and writes one .html file that can be opened by double-clicking.

⚙️ Key details

  • Supported Hosts: The skill works with Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Qoder, Factory Droid, Pi, Gemini CLI, Cline, Windsurf, and Amp.
  • Installation Methods:
    • When multiple roots resolve, the CLI recommends Symlink for a canonical copy linked into each root.
    • Pass --copy for independent copies per host.
    • A selection resolving to a single directory is copied.
    • Symlinks are unavailable on Windows without Developer Mode, so the CLI falls back to copies.
  • Updates and Migration:
    • Standalone installs require npx skills update diagram-design.
    • Marketplace installs follow native update paths.
    • Existing standalone copies must be removed before using marketplace commands to avoid conflicts.
  • Privacy: PRIVACY.md lists what the skill sends over the network.

🚀 Availability

Official builds come only from the repository. LittleMight, Cathryn Lavery’s company, publishes the plugin directory listings.

item.title: Mobile AI Factory Automates SLM Tuning for Android Devices
item.description:
Mobile AI Factory Automates SLM Tuning for Android Devices

A new system titled “Mobile AI Factory” was submitted on November 10, 2026. It automates the creation of specialized, quantized Small Language Models (SLMs) for Android devices.

🔍 Overview

Mobile AI Factory is an agentic system designed to build fine-tuned, quantized SLMs for specific tasks and phones. These models run locally, preserving user data privacy and functioning without connectivity.

🧩 How it works

The system uses an orchestrator LLM to decide whether to tune hyperparameters, mine real data, or generate synthetic examples. It employs fixed rules to roll back changes that negatively impact accuracy. The search process moves from small to large models and adapts its accuracy goals during the search.

⚙️ Key details

  • Search Strategy: Searches from small to large models across base models and quantizations.
  • Adaptation: Adapts its accuracy goal as it searches.
  • Hardware Awareness: Uses real measurements of the target phone across inference engines and backends.
  • Comparison: Without phone measurements, Claude Opus 5.5 misses requirements in 25% of easy and moderate cases and 60% of hard cases.

📊 Evaluation

The system was evaluated on ten tasks and four Android phones.

Evaluation Scope Details
Tasks 10
Devices 4 Android phones
  • Performance: On an unseen testset, its on-device models outperformed two five-shot frontier models on five tasks (by up to 0.34) and matched them on three more.
  • Efficiency: The search came within 0.03 of exhaustively training all 27 model variants on an entity extraction task, while using 19x less GPU time.
  • Hardware Dependency: The best configuration changes across phones.

🚀 Availability

Code for Mobile AI Factory is available at the provided URL.

item.title: Meta Updates Terms to Allow AI Training on Associated Websites
item.description:
Meta Updates Terms to Allow AI Training on Associated Websites

Meta has updated its terms of service to grant itself permission to crawl and scrape websites associated with business accounts for AI training. The new terms, which go into effect on October 30, allow Meta to use outside content to “develop, improve, research,” and “train” its AI products.

🔍 Overview

The policy applies to business accounts that promote their content across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger. It allows Meta to crawl all websites ‘associated’ with a business account. This includes domains, web pages, or URLs that are made available through the business’s use of Meta’s products and services.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Authorization: The terms authorize Meta to use automated software (such as web scrapers, bots, crawlers, and user agents) to access, index, cache, analyze, collect, retrieve, or crawl domains associated with products or services.
  • Usage: Meta may use any content from such domains to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of its Meta Company Products and services.
  • Enforcement: Businesses that do not agree to Meta’s new policies “may stop all access or use of our Products for business or commercial purposes.”

🧩 Legal and Industry Context

  • Robots.txt: Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts states there is “no change to how Meta uses web crawlers” and claims content owners can still use robots.txt flags to indicate their preferences.
  • Expert Analysis: Legal experts tell Nieman Lab that this could allow Meta to argue its commercial terms supersede other blocking instructions, like a site’s robots.txt file. This could potentially allow Meta to bypass a licensing agreement and freely train its AI models on content posted by online publishers.
  • Existing Deals: Meta has followed OpenAI in striking AI licensing deals with CNN, Fox News, USA Today, and People Inc., but these new terms could give the company access to a much broader swath of content.
  • Professor Quote: James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell, tells Nieman Lab that for news publishers, this clearly represents permission to Meta to train AI on any content from their sites and possibly to deploy some of that content, even in competition with the publishers themselves.

💡 Why It Matters

  • News Sites: The new policy may allow Meta to train AI on news sites for free.
  • Meta’s Stance: Andy Stone, Meta’s vice president of communications, writes in a post on X that this change isn’t meant to target news sites, stating the update is designed to pull accurate information about products for sale on third‑party websites when making on‑platform ad and content recommendations.
  • Cost Implications: Last month, Meta launched a new Meta One subscription that requires businesses and creators to pay to include links in posts and reels. Nieman Lab notes that “Meta has begun charging users to post links to the same content that it will be permitted to crawl for free.”

item.title: Wonderful Thailand CEO Discusses Scaling AI Agents at Techsauce 2026
item.description:
Wonderful Thailand CEO Discusses Scaling AI Agents at Techsauce 2026

Ariya Banomyong, President of Wonderful Thailand, addressed the challenge of moving AI from pilots to production at the Techsauce Global Summit 2026.

📈 Scaling from Pilots to Production

Most organizations are already running AI pilots, but few reach production. Banomyong stated that the constraint is rarely the technology itself, but how organizations are set up to design, deploy, and measure it. He noted that in previous technology cycles—internet adoption, e-commerce, and online video—the technology arrived as expected, and what differed was when organizations chose to act.

🧩 Architecture and Design Strategy

To scale effectively, organizations should avoid building separate agents within each function. Banomyong argued that the value of AI tends to appear across functions rather than within any one of them. When each department funds its own initiative and selects its own provider, the result can be several implementations that were never designed to work together. Solutions built for a sandbox are rarely ready for enterprise volumes or the wider set of use cases a business will want to run on the same foundation. Designing for production scale and multiple use cases from the outset, then piloting within that architecture, reduces later rebuilds.

📊 Use Case Examples

Banomyong illustrated successful deployments with two client examples:

Scenario Agents Involved Key Mechanism Outcome
SME Lending Relationship assistant, lending agent, credit reviewer Context sharing across agents; legacy system integration Chat message moves to booking in core system
Home Broadband Single assistant Camera reads router status lights Customer handled from start to finish without queue jumping

🛡️ Risk and Governance

On risk, Banomyong reframed the discussion around designing safeguards. In Wonderful’s architecture, an observer agent runs in the background to check that other agents operate within policy, governance, and regulatory requirements. Bank Hapoalim in Israel went live within three weeks at 88% containment, meaning roughly 880 of every 1,000 calls or chats were resolved without human involvement. Case studies on Wonderful’s website cite comparable results at 80% or above.

🚀 Company Updates

Wonderful operates in more than 35 markets and recently opened in Thailand with a local team. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Amsterdam, the company positions its product as an enterprise AI operating system. In September 2026, the company announced a $550 million Series C led by Insight Partners at a $5 billion valuation. The company was also named Official Enterprise AI Partner of FC Bayern in the same month.

⏱️ Delivery Timeline

Deployments generally take four to eight weeks, depending on workflow and integration complexity. Governance, guardrails, and evaluation tooling are in place from the start. Wonderful’s teams work directly with clients to redesign cross-functional workflows, then transfer capability to internal teams who build and manage agents on the same platform.

item.title: New Benchmark Evaluates LLM Agents in Enterprise Environments
item.description:
New Benchmark Evaluates LLM Agents in Enterprise Environments

LLM agents for enterprise systems of record cannot be evaluated on customer production data, and no existing substitute provides ground truth. To address this, researchers present the Era by Eon Benchmark for evaluating LLM agents that use enterprise tools.

🔍 Overview

The benchmark is built around a complete fictional company. It includes product simulators, company-specific internal databases, benchmark questions, and computed answer keys. Industry, company size, business model, application portfolio, and a seed define each company. One seeded entity graph supplies shared company data to simulators of Salesforce, Zendesk, Slack, Gong, and other products.

Company Definition Attributes

Attribute Role in Benchmark
Industry Defines the sector
Company Size Defines the scale
Business Model Defines revenue generation
Application Portfolio Defines the software stack
Seed Defines the starting state

⚙️ How it works

A questionconditioned generator creates the schemas and records for internal databases. It takes shared entities, keys, and values from the same graph before generating database-specific facts. Both mechanisms therefore describe one consistent enterprise estate. Every expected answer is computed from the final records, so grading is exact. Design and answer-key checks validate the internal databases. A realism scorecard and adversarial detector validate the entity graph.

📊 Results

Across 23 generated companies, the mean realism score rose from 61.8 to 97.0, with zero records flagged as synthetic. In the reported simulator-track comparison, nine models answered the same 33 questions three times each. Accuracy estimates ranged from 42.4% to 76.8%, and three of 36 pairwise differences remained supported after correction.

💾 Database Normalization

We introduce a Database Normalization Benchmark (DNBENCH), comprising 3,275 samples for evaluating LLM-driven database normalization from 1NF to BCNF. DNBENCH uses a three-axis protocol to measure semantic equivalence, structural accuracy, and logical validity. Across Single, Complex, and Real World levels, DNBENCH uncovers recurring failures in dependency inference, schema decomposition, and inter-table constraint reconstruction.

🤖 Multi-Agent Reasoning

We further propose Multi-Agent Reasoning for Schemas (MARS), which separates evidence extraction, violation diagnosis, and decomposition planning from schema generation and verification. MARS improves the DNB-SCORE by 82.0% over the single-prompt baseline.
